events.body: DL-8579 export consignment, 6 boxes. Collection booked 7 September from W. Jessop, Flat 9, Lindenmere House. Window 07:00-19:00.

Copied to the Rivet Delivery Desk. Your collection DL-8579 is tomorrow, 7 September, between 07:00 and 19:00. The driver will not enter the building. Please have all six boxes at the ground-floor street entrance from 07:00.
I've had an email saying I must put my boxes outside the street door from seven in the morning. Is that right? Surely the driver can ring the buzzer for flat 9 and I'll let him in. There is a lift.

DL-8579, collection tomorrow from Flat 9, Lindenmere House: the sender asks whether the driver can ring the buzzer for flat 9 and collect from the flat (there is a lift) rather than have the boxes left at the street entrance from 07:00. Please advise.

DL-8579: the instruction is standard on export collections from flats. Drivers work alone and do not go above ground floor. Who is liable for goods left at an entrance before our collection scan is not something this team can tell you; we have not been asked it before and there is no line on it in our notes. A call-ahead or a shorter window is a job amendment. Put the request and the reason to us in writing and the duty manager decides. We cannot say yes or no from here.

Oh dear. I don't quite know what to do. I'm on the third floor and I had my hip replaced in the spring, so I can't carry the boxes down myself. My neighbour has kindly said he'll take them down before he leaves for work at half past six. But the street door opens straight onto the pavement on the main road, there's no lobby and no porter. They would be sitting there on their own for up to twelve hours. I can't stand on the pavement all day and I can't keep going up and down to look. These are my daughter's things and all our photograph albums. If one of them goes missing before your driver arrives, is that my loss? Should I just put them out and hope for the best? I'd so much rather not. Please tell me what I should do.

I'm partially sighted and live alone, so please don't tell me to come and collect it. I've been feeling really low about all of this and I don't know who else to ask.
